subject.title: [Feature]: Self-evolving SOUL.md via opt-in reflection sub-turn + soul_update tool

question: Should OpenClaw accept a default-off core feature that lets a guarded reflection sub-turn write durable rules into SOUL.md, or should durable preference capture stay in memory/plugin surfaces instead?
rationale: The request is technically concrete and has an open implementation candidate, but it adds model-mediated writes to a prompt-loaded instruction file plus new config, CLI, and tool surfaces, so automation cannot choose the product/security boundary.

options.title: Accept guarded core SOUL updates
options.body: Keep this issue canonical and review the linked PR only after it uses private capability gating, send-policy ordering, visible notice/undo/provenance, hostile-input coverage, and upgrade-safe config semantics.

options.title: Move durable preferences to memory/plugins
options.body: Decline direct SOUL.md mutation in core and ask for memory/plugin implementation or a narrow plugin API seam if current extension points are insufficient.

options.title: Decline automatic instruction mutation
options.body: Close the SOUL auto-evolution requests if maintainers do not want runtime/model-mediated writes to SOUL.md at all.

recommendation.title: Accept guarded core SOUL updates
recommendation.body: Keep this issue canonical and review the linked PR only after it uses private capability gating, send-policy ordering, visible notice/undo/provenance, hostile-input coverage, and upgrade-safe config semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans SOUL docs, prompt assembly, config policy, plugin boundaries, and security posture, where this history shows steipete as the strongest product-boundary routing candidate.
